To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the zinc finger domain of Nab2 is required for poly(A) tail regulation and is critical for the proper formation of mRNA 3′ ends.
the polyadenosine recognition domain of Nab is composed of three tandem zinc finger motifs and that this recognition domain is essential for proper mRNA 3′ end processing.
the polyadenosine recognition domain of Nab 2 is required for the proper control of polyadenylation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanisms by which RNA is regulated in eukaryotic cells.
the role that polyadenosine-binding proteins play in the regulation of mRNA metabolism.
the role that Nab2 plays in regulating the poly(A) tails of mRNA transcripts.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Nab2 polyadenosine binding activity is required for correct 3′- end formation of mRNA.
the poly(A) RNA binding domain of Nab2 is required for proper control of mRNA 3′ end formation.
Nab2 binds to RNA, that this binding is important for the function of the mRNA 2′-O-methyltransferase Trf4, and that this binding is critical for proper poly(A) tail formation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
poly(A) tail control is a critical step in the coupling of mRNA 3′ processing and nuclear export.
poly(A) tail control is a critical step in the coupled process of mRNA 3′ end formation.
Nab2 is required to couple polyadenosine tail length to mRNA 3′ end processing.
The main takeaway from our work is that
polyadenosine binding is important for proper control of mRNA 3′ end formation in vivo, and that this function is separable from the nuclear poly(A) RNA export function of Nab2.
Nab2 is a bona fide poly(A)-binding protein that is required for the control of poly(A)-tail length in yeast.
Nab2 is a poly(A) binding protein that plays an essential role in mRNA 3′ end formation.
